description: The state flower: a mound of blue-green, finely cut leaves with silky orange cups, each on its own stalk, that open in the sun and close at dusk and in cloud; 15-50 cm tall. It flowers on open, sunny, well-drained ground from March into May, brightest on the south-facing grassy slopes and road banks, and a single plant may flower on into summer where the soil holds water.

season_notes.winter: A small rosette of ferny grey-green leaves after the rains.
season_notes.spring: Orange cups from March, most in April; closed in the morning cold and the evening, wide open at noon.
season_notes.summer: Long thin seed pods split and fling the seeds; the plant dries to a few pale stalks.
season_notes.fall: Gone, but for seed in the ground waiting for rain.

notes: California poppy grows throughout the foothills in grassland, oak savanna, chaparral openings and on disturbed banks, on open sunny ground; in the hot interior it behaves as a winter annual, germinating with the fall rains, making a rosette, flowering March-May and dying back by July (coastal plants are perennial). The leaves are blue-green and dissected into narrow lobes (leaf shape ferny, 4-8 cm); the flowers are four-petalled cups 3-6 cm across, deep orange in spring and paler yellow-orange on late flowers, one per stalk, held above the mound; the fruit a slender 5-8 cm capsule. The animals barely touch it (it is bitter): deer take a few leaves in spring, quail and ground squirrels the seed, so its food relations are few and its value is as the colour of the spring slopes. habitat: sun (shade 0), south and steep slopes above north ones, road verges and old fields x1.6.
